title: Quantification of Strain in a Porcine Model of Skin Expansion Using Multi-View Stereo and Isogeometric Kinematics
protocol: Acclimate one-month-old male Yucatan mini pigs to standard housing for one week.
Feed the acclimated pigs ad libitum.
Anesthetize the animal using ketamine/acepromazine for induction (4 - 6 mg/kg).
Continue anesthesia with isoflurane for maintenance.
Monitor palpebral reflex to evaluate depth of anesthesia.
Monitor vital signs including heart rate, body temperature, respiratory rate, and response to pinch by tissue forceps.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes to protect against corneal abrasions.
Administer pre-procedural antibiotics.
Clean the dorsal skin with chlorhexidine-based surgical soap.
Transfer four 10 x 10 cm2 grids using tattoo transfer medium, placing two on each side of the animal.
Wash the area on the animal where the grid is to be placed with isopropyl rubbing alcohol.
Apply the grid directly onto the skin with the pen-ink side down.
Inject local anesthetic (1% lidocaine with 1:100,000 epinephrine) subcutaneously at the site of each planned incision.
Make an incision on either side of the animal in the midpoint between the two grids.
Use a hemostat to develop a subcutaneous tunnel beneath the grid of interest.
Insert the expander beneath the grid through the developed tunnel.
Place the port for expander inflation remotely along the dorsal midline through a subcutaneous tunnel.
Repair wounds by suturing.
Treat animals with prophylactic antibiotics via intramuscular injection (Ceftiofur 5 mg/kg IM once).
Provide analgesics via intramuscular injection every 12 h for 4 doses (Buprenorphine 0.05 - 0.1 mg/kg).
Observe animals continuously postoperatively, including routine measurement of vital signs.
Resume animal ambulation and maintain normothermia before transferring to a separate cage.
Monitor until the animal can walk independently on all four legs.
Check animals daily for wound healing evaluation.
Remove sutures 14 days postoperatively.
Sedate the animal by administering ketamine (4 - 6 mg/kg) and dexmedetomidine at 20 - 80 µg/kg before each inflation step.
Perform five inflation steps at 0, 2, 7, 10, and 15 days to achieve filling volumes of 50, 75, 105, 165, and 225 cc respectively.
Reverse dexmedetomidine with atipamezole (1:1 volume:volume) if necessary.
Administer isoflurane via mask ventilation following ketamine/acepromazine induction for general anesthesia if required.
Attach two plastic flexible tape measures to the skin of the animal using surgical tape, placing them between the grids on the left and right sides.
Position the camera above the animal and leaning towards the caudal side to capture a shot where the tattooed grids are fully visible.
Move in a circular pattern around the animal from caudal to rostral direction.
Take photographs ensuring tattooed grids appear entirely in the frame.
Maximize space that the grids occupy in each photograph.
Position camera towards ventral side and take photographs in an arch from ventral to dorsal region.
Place the animal on the opposite side.
Take 30 photographs of the remaining grids following previous steps.
Find the remote filling port.
Inject required amount of sterile 0.9% injectable saline solution for expansion protocol.
Locate the ports and prep over the skin of the animal with isopropyl alcohol wipes.
Access the port with a sterile 25-gauge butterfly needle attached to a syringe filled with sterile injectable saline.
Inject the desired amount of saline solution.
Administer general anesthesia by delivering isoflurane via mask ventilation following ketamine/acepromazine induction.
Evaluate depth of anesthesia by monitoring the palpebral reflex.
Monitor vital signs (heart rate, body temperature, respiratory rate, and/or response to pinch with tissue forceps).
Euthanize the animal by intravenous overdose of pentobarbital 90 - 100 mg/kg.
Confirm death by the absence of detectable heartbeat using a pulse oximeter and pulse palpation as well as the absence of spontaneous respirations.
